Maya (AE): Heads-up — Acadia Health wants a 6-week POC. They'll bring a finetuned artifact (acadia-clinical-0.9.pt). Main asks: can we run int4 variants on Dedicated or Private, estimate pricing and timelines, and list any compliance blockers (PHI?).

Ethan (SalesEng): Do we know the model format? HF-ish or plain torch state dict? Any custom CUDA ops they compiled?

Sam (SolutionsEng): Pulled the artifact from the deal S3. It's a PyTorch state_dict wrapped with a huggingface-style config + tokenizer. No compiled/custom ops in the package. Running compatibility scan now.

deploy-bot: model-compat-scan queued for acadia-clinical-0.9 (id: scan-2026-03-21-ACD-01)

Sam (SolutionsEng): scan results:
- detected format: pytorch + transformers metadata
- custom ops: none
- embeddings/rotary: rotary embeddings present (rotary -> check int4 kernel support)
- quantization suggestions: fp16 baseline, int8 recommended; int4 possible but requires calibration & QA on clinical samples
- attention kernels: flash-attn available on H100; fallback to tiled-attn otherwise (degrade perf for >2k contexts)
- KV cache memory estimate @4k context: ~36GB per model instance (with optimizer offload disabled)

Ethan (SalesEng): Good — 36GB KV cache means a single H100-80GB node could host the model for 4k contexts with some overhead. For HA and throughput we'd suggest 2 nodes. Any rough $ numbers for POC (6 weeks)?

Sam (SolutionsEng): Back-of-envelope POC pricing (6 weeks):
- Dedicated reserved (1x H100 pool, 30/7 uptime): ~$9,000/month (so ~$13,500 for 6 weeks)
- Dedicated reserved (2x H100 pool for redundancy/throughput): ~$16,500/month (~$24,750 for 6 weeks)
- PAYG-hosted equivalent (no reserved commits): ~ $0.28 per 1k tokens served (very workload dependent)
- Typical caching & batching improvements: 20-30% token cost reduction if we enable prefix/KV caching + aggressive batching where latency allows

Maya (AE): Customer says training corpus was de-identified but some original identifiers remain in a small subset. They want the fastest path that remains compliant.

Jordan (Security): If thereis any chance of re-identifiable PHI in training/inference, our compliance baseline demands either Private deployment (VPC or on-prem) or Dedicated with an executed HIPAA Business Associate Agreement + network isolation. Additional requirements: KMS for envelope encryption, SIEM forwarding for audit trails, and DLP/redaction controls for outputs if they request.

Maya (AE): They prefer Dedicated for simplicity, but can do Private if needed. What's the lead time on a Dedicated + BA?

Jordan (Security): Typical timeline: 2-3 weeks to provision Dedicated and complete BA/legal signoff (assuming procurement is responsive). Private VPC/on-prem -> 3-5 weeks depending on infra access and creds. If they want immediate validation, we can spin an ephemeral Private deployment inside their VPC (shorter ops window) but need their infra contact and least-privileged creds.

Ethan (SalesEng): They also asked about experimenting with quant variants during the POC (fp16 -> int8 -> int4) without downtime. Can runtime handle hot swaps?

Sam (SolutionsEng): Yes, runtime supports variant pinning and canary traffic. Typical flow: upload variant, create a canary route at 5-10% traffic, validate outputs against a calibration set, then promote. Example commands:

```
# upload variant
redwoodctl models upload --model acadia-clinical --file acadia-clinical-int4.pt --variant int4-calib
# create canary route at 10%
redwoodctl routes create --model acadia-clinical --variant int4-calib --traffic 0.10
# promote to default
redwoodctl routes promote --route acadia-clinical:int4-calib --to default
```

Sam (SolutionsEng): Notes: rotary embeddings sometimes require special handling in int4 kernels; please run the calibration dataset (we'll need ~200 representative clinical examples) to measure token-level accuracy drop.

Jordan (Security): Also flagging contract items: audit log retention (customer requested 5 years), SIEM forwarding endpoint, and requirement for KMS customer-managed keys if Private. I'll prepare a BA/DLP addendum draft.

Maya (AE): Thanks. Can someone open the ops ticket and attach the scan artifact + suggested calibration set? Also we need a short integration snippet to share with their engineers.

Sam (SolutionsEng): Created ticket OPS-1338 "acadia-poc-compat" and uploaded scan artifact (scan-2026-03-21-ACD-01). Calibration dataset placeholder uploaded to the ticket (we'll ask them to replace with real samples).

Sam (SolutionsEng): Quick curl example for integration (replace MODEL_ID and API_KEY):

```
curl -X POST "https://api.redwood.ai/v1/models/MODEL_ID:predict" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $API_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"inputs":"Extract problem list from clinical note: ...","max_tokens":256,"temperature":0.0}'
```

Ethan (SalesEng): I'll draft the POC statement of work with both Dedicated + Private options and include the rough pricing. Maya — do you want me to include a note about calibration runs for int4 accuracy?

Maya (AE): Yes please. Also ask their infra lead for a timeline and whether they prefer KMS with their key. I'll send a summary to the customer and schedule an intro call with their infra/security lead.

Jordan (Security): I'll draft the BA + DLP checklist and share a first pass in this thread. :ok_hand:

Sam (SolutionsEng): Scheduling a perf run once infra is up. Keep me posted on infra creds.

Maya (AE): Great work team. I'll update the deal and confirm next steps with Acadia. :sparkles:
